name: Asylum -- Refugee Status Determination

qualifying_event.description: A person with a well-founded fear of persecution may apply for refugee status through Botswana's domestic refugee status determination process, run by the newly established Commissioner for Refugees and the Botswana Refugees Committee under a 2024 Refugees Act, replacing the earlier Refugees (Recognition and Control) Act of 1968. Botswana is party to the 1951 Refugee Convention, its 1967 Protocol, and the 1969 OAU Convention.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Application to the Commissioner for Refugees; identity documents where available.

requirements.blocker_text: Well-founded fear of persecution meeting the 1951 Convention / 1967 Protocol / 1969 OAU Convention refugee definitions, assessed through a four-tier determination process.
Application filed with the Commissioner for Refugees.
requirements.fix_path: File a refugee status application with the Commissioner for Refugees.

sources.title: UNHCR Regional Information and Analysis Mapping Platform (RIMAP) -- Botswana: party to the 1951 Convention/1967 Protocol/1969 OAU Convention; a 2024 Refugees Act introduced a four-tier government-led RSD process with a Commissioner for Refugees and Botswana Refugees Committee, replacing the 1968 Act; primary population hosted at Dukwi Refugee Camp (~580km from Gaborone), with smaller urban populations in Gaborone and Francistown

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Botswana). STATUS: DRAFT -- LIVE LEGAL TRANSITION FLAG: Botswana passed a new Refugees Act in 2024 replacing the 1968 Refugees (Recognition and Control) Act with a genuine domestic four-tier RSD process and new institutions (Commissioner for Refugees, Botswana Refugees Committee) -- this is a significant structural upgrade from the older, more UNHCR-dependent model many secondary sources (written before 2024) still describe. Modeled here per the NEW framework, sourced to UNHCR's own regional mapping platform (tier-2, intergovernmental) rather than a Botswana government gazette publication of the new Act itself, which was not reached in this pass -- exact timelines, work-rights-while-pending policy, and camp-vs-urban-settlement rules under the new Act were not confirmed and are disclosed as gaps. This is a materially different shape from Jordan's UNHCR-administered-under-MOU system (see jo_international_protection.json): Botswana now has its own domestic refugee law and government institutions running RSD directly, not an externally-run process substituting for domestic law.
